paragraphs: Athena Security sells concealed weapons detection systems together with the software that runs a screening program around them. The Apollo 500 is described as an AI powered system built for entrances that need high throughput, consistent detection of dangerous items and a low alarm rate. The company also offers an X-ray baggage scanner whose computer vision is said to identify firearms, knives, explosives and 3D-printed weapons.

The software layer is meant to add accountability, visibility and control on top of the physical detector rather than replace it. It is built to sit over detection hardware from several manufacturers instead of a single proprietary line. Athena states that its logging covers DHS prohibited items records, equipment testing records and secondary screening procedures. For facilities in California, the company says the system supports compliance with a state law on weapons detection.

The settings named on the site are healthcare providers, casinos, schools and warehouse distribution facilities across North America. Published case studies include one on a casino in Pennsylvania. The site also carries a notice that no technology can guarantee complete accuracy or prevent every incident.

quote.text: While the system is designed to enhance security and improve threat detection, no technology can guarantee 100% accuracy or prevention of all incidents.
